items.summary_html: Apple's new HomeView device is a seven-inch tablet that starts at $299. It can recognize up to six members of a household and change its content based on who is using it. There is a countertop version and a version that can be mounted on a wall. The HomeView will be available for purchase starting on November 13.
items.title: Apple Introduces HomeView, a $299 Tablet for the Home (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google's flagship Gemini 4 Argon multimodal language AI model is now broadly available. Developers and enterprises now have a powerful new option for software engineering, financial analysis, legal work, cybersecurity, and scientific research. API prices have been discounted substantially for a limited time. Argon is available through the paid Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Antigravity, eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions, and to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers through the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.
items.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Argon broadly available with limited-time low API pricing of 2/10 per 1M token (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX plans to perform as many as 456 launches and 912 landings at its Texas facility each year. The company's CEO, Elon Musk, has been open about the company's intent to launch Starship as rapidly as possible in the future. He has claimed that, in less than a decade, SpaceX will be able to launch Starship more than once every hour. SpaceX recently announced plans to invest as much as $100 billion to build a massive launch site in southern Louisiana to support rapid Starship launches.
items.title: SpaceX Plan to Launch 456 Starships a Year in Texas Under Review (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Science Corporation's vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, is commercially available in Europe for patients who have lost their sight to an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, but the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases. It recently implanted the chip in a patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. The company's work with PRIMA is part of a broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface. It envisions a future where BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications rather than just being used to control computers.
items.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: There are four types of ambition. Speed gets the same work done in less time. Altitude involves going up in abstraction and considering the outcome rather than the individual task. Depth considers a task the way a field-leading expert would, going one level deeper and touching the underlying data, tools, and problems. Range draws on multiple fields rather than just the one the task might need at the surface using knowledge, tools, and techniques you normally wouldn't.
items.title: How to be more ambitious: A tutorial for humans with models (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic was being bottlenecked by developer infrastructure built for human scale, so it built an in-house version control system called Scion to support its next stage of growth, and fully migrated its monorepo from git in five months. It also built and shipped a code review surface, code search, a rich source control IAM system, novel ways of managing and landing large amounts of reviewed code, and more, all in that same time period. Anthropic averaged about 2,500 code changes merged per day in May. It now merges over 30,000 per day, and the rate of growth isn't expected to slow down anytime soon.
items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic (23 minute read)

items.summary_html: Blue-collar workers typically do the hands-on labor of making or fixing stuff. Software developers have tried to separate themselves from this category, but they also make or fix stuff, just in bits rather than atoms. Just like electricians or carpenters, software developers must spend years practicing their craft in order to become skilled and sought-after. Just like anyone else in a skilled trade, software engineers can be outpaced by technology.
items.title: Were we blue-collar workers all along? (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI discovered a hidden recording device in one of its offices recently. It was traced to Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi Arabian national who joined the company's product team in July 2025 as an engineer. He was arrested by the FBI. The device was built to evade detection and used advanced encryption. It could monitor audio and had a way to transfer data without being noticed.
items.title: FBI Arrests OpenAI Employee Accused of Planting Bug in Office (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cloudflare's data pipeline handles roughly two billion events per second while hardware capacity grows more slowly than traffic. Product-specific schemas, zstd compression, later replication, earlier sampling, and aggregation have collectively deferred the equivalent of two and a half years of hardware expansion.
items.title: Rewinding the Exponential: How We Keep Hardware Usage Down (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic replaced Git with Scion after daily merges grew from roughly 2,500 to more than 30,000. The centralized system uses server-side commits, sparse checkouts, and layered caches, reducing its source control infrastructure's CPU and memory footprint by 200 times and freeing 25% of CI CPU capacity.
items.title: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Relace explains how it built a small model that applies code edits at a reported 10,000 tokens per second using high-quality merge data, LoRA fine-tuning, FP8 quantization, and speculative decoding. Its training pipeline filtered 200,000 candidate examples down to about 145,000, using a judge calibrated against 500 manually reviewed merges. Relace Apply 3 supports a 256,000-token context and multiple diff formats, although improving frontier-model edit accuracy could eventually reduce the need for specialized apply models.
items.title: A Year of Fast Apply: The Path to 10k Tokens per Second (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Programming for curiosity and enjoyment can restore motivation without requiring a business case or a finished product. This presentation suggests small experiments, toy implementations, language exploration, and documenting the process, with permission to switch projects or stop when they stop being fun.
items.title: Recreational Programming (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: More ambitious AI use can mean pursuing higher-level outcomes, applying expert methods to raw data, or combining ideas from multiple fields. Practical examples show how to move beyond generating a quarterly slide deck toward identifying urgent decisions, testing assumptions, and validating results with independent tools.
items.title: How to Be More Ambitious: A Tutorial for Humans with Models (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: TanStack Start 1.0 is now stable and ready for production, formalizing a commitment to its APIs after extensive real-world use. It combines type-safe routing with server rendering, typed server functions, and middleware spanning client and server, while shipping current agent guidance through TanStack Intent.
items.title: TanStack Start 1.0 Is Stable (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini 4 Argon for complex software engineering, scientific research, robotics, and professional workflows. The model offers a one-million-token output window, and Google reports uses ranging from large Chromium refactors to physics-ready robot simulations and vulnerability remediation.
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon (Website)

Early partners independently improved policies across manufacturing and other applications, although some deployments exposed network connectivity challenges.
items.title: Frontier Models for Every Robot: Announcing the Pi API Beta (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Two-thirds of the Forbes AI 50 companies use some form of usage-based pricing as variable AI costs push businesses toward hybrid subscriptions, credits, and outcome charges. Examples from AI companies show why spending controls, flexible packaging, measurable customer value, and pricing pages readable by both people and agents are becoming part of the product.
items.title: The “Alien” Economics of AI Monetization (6 minute read)

OpenAI says it referred the discovery to the FBI and has found no indication that model weights, source code, or customer data were improperly accessed or taken.
items.title: OpenAI Engineer Arrested over Alleged Conference Room Bugging (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: In ten runs on one Java API service, a behavioral harness raised GPT-6 Luna's acceptance rate from three successes to ten, while GPT-6 Sol passed all ten runs with or without it. Harnessed Luna cost about 33% less per run than unharnessed Sol, but those estimates exclude harness maintenance and the unusually detailed brief limits how broadly the results apply.
items.title: Are Harnesses Worth the Cost? (20 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI Employee Arrested Over Hidden Recording Device (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google made Gemini 4 Argon available on Google Cloud as a frontier model for long, multi-step enterprise work. It was positioned for tasks requiring sustained context and domain expertise, including software development, finance, legal work, and cybersecurity.
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon Lands on Google Cloud (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The debate over AI consciousness continues with minimal progress, as many argue without strong evidence. Anthropic's new policy classifies abusive behavior towards AI, such as Claude, as a violation of terms to cultivate positive model interactions. Despite skepticism from many, some, including Nick Bostrom, believe current AIs may be conscious, complicating ethical considerations around AI development.
items.title: Arguments About AI Consciousness Remain Highly Motivated and At Best Overconfident (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Splitting a task among several AI agents creates another job: deciding who does what, passing information between them, and checking their results. Anthropic's dynamic workflows let Claude write the program that manages those steps. An October 12 demonstration assigned stock tickers to separate agents, then reviewed their findings before producing a report. The presenters said this found more detail but cost much more than using one agent. Developers can set a session spending limit, but the running model does not know that budget.
items.title: How Anthropic's Dynamic Workflows Coordinate Claude Agents (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24B-parameter reasoning model with 2B active parameters, is designed for fast, private on-device agents. It outperforms or matches larger models like Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on five out of eight benchmarks and runs up to 1.7x faster due to its efficient architecture. Available on Hugging Face, it supports extensive inference frameworks, making it suitable for tasks needing swift local inference and tool usage.
items.title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nvidia is making the full NVIDIA Run:ai platform available as open-source software. It is now possible for every NVIDIA DSX ecosystem partner and AI cloud to increase workload throughput, improve GPU utilization, and operate shared AI infrastructure more efficiently and effectively. The release includes the complete NVIDIA Run:ai platform, KAI Scheduler, GPU Fractioning Operator, KAI Resource Management, and Workload Map. Platform teams and ecosystem partners can adopt NVIDIA Run:ai as an integrated whole, build on it for their own products and services, or integrate individual components based on their requirements.
items.title: NVIDIA Run:ai Is Now Open Source as Part of NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Physical Intelligence is making its latest models available for training and inference through the Pi API beta. The Pi API adapts the latest and most powerful robotic foundation models to each application, dealing with ML infrastructure, compute, and complex data pipelines. Users just upload data, launch fine-tuning on managed compute and infrastructure, and access the fine-tuned models via a hosted gateway to run inference.
items.title: Frontier Models for Every Robot (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenCode 2.0 contains quite a lot of new features, performance improvements, and bug fixes. The server now automatically runs as a single background process. Programmatic clients will autodiscover the local service and just work. OpenCode can now be used as a library with the SDK package. More details about the update are available in the article.
items.title: OpenCode 2.0 (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ramp has launched Glass, an AI workspace that shares company knowledge, reusable skills, and collaborative sessions across teams. Employees have made 6,500+ knowledge edits, while model routing cut AI costs by 30% and automated workflows dramatically expanded feature-request tracking.
items.title: Ramp Glass (4 minute read)

Helion, part of an upcoming open blueprint by AMD for OCP, is set for release in November.
items.title: Introducing AMD Helion, Agentic AI Compute at Rack Scale (10 minute read)

The next-generation Maia 300 uses compute chiplets on TSMC's N2P process and targets long-context, multi-step agent workloads. Digitimes reports that the supply chain is already preparing for a surge in server builds in 2027.
items.title: Microsoft takes Maia to multi-gigawatt scale, making it the default inference chip for its own products (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: This deep dive uses the Emmy compiler framework to follow PyTorch operations down to CUDA one lowering stage at a time: Tensor IR, Loop IR, Tile IR, Kernel IR, and finally emitted code. It uses RMSNorm and matrix multiplication as worked examples. It also covers operator fusion, schedule selection, and online attention rewrites, so readers can see what Triton-style stacks do under the hood.
items.title: Building a GPU compiler from scratch, from PyTorch to CUDA (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Physical Intelligence opened a beta API for its π robotics foundation models: upload demonstrations, fine-tune on Pi-managed compute, and run the result on your own robot through a hosted inference gateway. Early partners spanned hardware from Actor's autonomous wheel loader, running a commercial deployment with no operator onboard, to Almond's dual-arm Axol, which learned to deburr its own spacers in four days. Since most ran cloud-hosted inference, network connectivity was a pain point for some.
items.title: Physical Intelligence opens a beta API to fine-tune and host π robot models (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple Silicon Macs have powerful GPUs that sit mostly idle in normal use. Minions combines them across machines into a virtual GPU cloud for large ML inference jobs, with fault tolerance and flexible task scheduling. The pitch is that teams can use hardware they already own instead of waiting for expensive, centralized GPU capacity.
items.title: Apple's Minions pools idle Macs into a virtual GPU cloud (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team ran Gemma4-26B-A4B across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes with 4GB of RAM each, using pipeline parallelism at 0.39 tokens per second, to test whether small models could replicate across cheap IoT hardware. A 9B model got inference running on 8 of 9 hardware types tested, and a Kimwolf-sized botnet would total only about 40 H100s of compute. By their trend line, small models reach the needed capability in simplified tests by year-end.
items.title: Anthropic runs a 26B model across 15 $55 TV boxes to test IoT self-replication (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: An Abilene-scale build requires roughly $17B for chips and servers, $3B for power, and only $2.4B for construction. Transformers, generators, and cooling equipment face long lead times and rising prices.
items.title: What a 1GW AI data center costs: about $30B, and $17B of it is chips (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple's Home Collection, built with LG and Schneider Electric, covers cameras, thermostats, sensors, a doorbell, and a deadbolt. LG's lock uses Ultra Wideband to unlock as you approach and works locally over Matter and Aliro, while its indoor cam physically tilts away when someone's home. Every device supports Thread, and cameras keep recording to built-in storage if Wi-Fi drops. Prices run $199.95 to $399.95, with availability starting in December.
items.title: Apple Home Collection brings LG and Schneider cameras, a lock, and thermostats to Apple Home (3 minute read)

Its immediate predecessor is the best-selling nonmobile game of all time. The game's release is causing other entertainment companies to delay products until next year because they know GTA VI will suck up the planet's attention for most of November. It will almost certainly be the most expensive video game ever created. This article looks at how Rockstar Games built what is expected to be the biggest video game blockbuster of all time.
items.title: The Making of Grand Theft Auto VI (28 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic told investors recently that the company's revenue for the third quarter jumped about 45% from the prior quarter to $16.8 billion. The AI lab is currently pursuing what may become the largest-ever initial public offering. Its IPO could value the company at $2 trillion. The San Francisco company is expected to begin trading as early as next month. A successful launch from Anthropic could reopen the door for other listings and provide a vote of confidence for the industry.
items.title: Anthropic Says Revenue Jumped 45% to $16.8 Billion in Third Quarter (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: NASA's Perseverance rover has now driven 28.1 miles on Mars' surface, surpassing the distance that Opportunity covered from 2004 to 2018. Perseverance landed on Mars in February 2021 and has been traveling in and around the Jezero Crater since. It was set to surpass the driving record back in August, but it came across some interesting rocks, so it dawdled for two months. Perseverance most likely still has many miles to go in the coming years. This article contains some of the highlights from its drive so far.
items.title: 28 Miles and Counting: NASA's Perseverance Rover Sets a Mars Driving Record (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Two NASA missions are on track to launch to Venus in the early 2030s. The Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging (DAVINCI), which will send a parachute-assisted descent probe through Venus' atmosphere, is now scheduled for launch in December 2030. The Venus Emissivity, Radio science, InSAR, Topography, And Spectroscopy (VERITAS) mission will launch in November 2032 to map the Venusian surface by radar from orbit. The European Space Agency is building an orbiter for launch to Venus in 2032, and Rocket Lab plans to launch a privately funded probe as soon as next year to search for signs of organic material in the planet's clouds.
items.title: Things are finally looking up for NASA's first missions to Venus in a generation (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Being able to tell clean code from messy code is still useful, but it's becoming something that tools can help with. Knowing what shape a program should have before anyone writes it is something AI still can't do yet. The best way to get better at AI coding might be to spend more time thinking about problems and less time thinking about prompts. The programmers that get the most out of these tools already knew what they wanted.
items.title: Code you didn't write (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Giving AI agents a way to independently verify their work heavily improves the quality of output. Write end-to-end tests that simulate real user flows and act as the ground truth. Use property-based testing to specify what should never happen and generate thousands of test cases that attempt to break those constraints. Require tests to run quickly and deterministically so that agents retry when the loop is slow or unreliable.
items.title: Agentic Verification (18 minute read)

The growth in new AI customers has slowed down significantly. Growth in the market will now have to come from more intense adoption rather than more customers.

items.summary_html: Browsers fetch lazy-loaded media at different distances, with Chrome adjusting its margin based on connection speed, Firefox using a fixed 600-pixel threshold, and Safari applying a viewport-based threshold to images. The article explains why the largest contentful paint image should load eagerly and why media dimensions should be reserved to prevent layout shifts. Its practical takeaway is to use native lazy loading selectively, based on how far ahead each browser fetches.
items.title: Lazy Loading Images and Media: How Far Ahead Browsers Fetch (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: GitHub rebuilt its star-history API to return up to 30 weeks of daily counts in one request. Maintainers can track a project's momentum without exposing stargazer identities, which could be scraped for spam or phishing. To avoid simply shifting the cost to count queries, the endpoint filters stars by time before counting, reducing database work.
items.title: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: The article revisits the idea that UI should be a pure function of state and explains why it matters for agent-written interfaces. Passing roles, plans, billing status, and feature flags explicitly lets teams render and inspect each state combination before release.
items.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era (6 minute read)

The response argues that passkeys remain more phishing-resistant than TOTP and recommends continuing to use them.
items.title: Passkeys Are Not a Trap (4 minute read)

items.title: Grok Voice 3.0 (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Jev 1.14.0 features image support, a new type, and longer context. Multimodal support has also been turned on for Jev 1.13.0. Both models perform worse on multimodality than on pure text. Breaking down questions into the simplest possible decompositions helps a lot. The new 'box' type returns a single bounding box. It is a preview of TypeSafe's explorations beyond simple decisions and into what else System One Models can support.
items.title: Jev: For the builders AND dreamers (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Gavin Baker expects open-weight specialist models and frontier systems to coexist behind routers, reducing model margins while increasing compute demand. He argues existing infrastructure commitments remain financeable and warns that excessive concentration or overbuilding poses greater risks.
items.title: A Hybrid, Multi-Model AI Future (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI has made producing code cheap. This moves the bottleneck of software delivery to deciding, verifying, and coordinating. AI amplifies whatever coordination an organization already had. Adding more agents will not fix weak coordination, just as adding more developers never did.
items.title: More Agents, Same Mythical Month (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google Research's Harness² lets agents iteratively improve their prompts, tools, memory, and orchestration without changing model weights. It refines the harness for each task and then carries evidence-backed lessons forward to improve future tasks.

items.summary_html: Google's Deep Review is an agent AI system engineer designed to provide rigorous feedback and technical verification on complex documents. It was initially designed for computer science academic paper analysis, but its capabilities have since expanded to reviewing documents across many domains. Deep Review will initially support PDFs and plain text as input formats, but support for multi-file inputs will arrive soon. Google believes that tools like Deep Review will play a significant role across the peer review process in the coming years by empowering both authors and reviewers.

items.summary_html: Routers have emerged as a new primitive of the AI stack. They promise to handle the complexity of model management and help companies benefit from new models without revisiting model selection across every application themselves. Every router shares the same fundamental design, but they differ in how they decide. This post provides an independent comparison of current routers and looks at how today's routers compare with single models on quality and cost.
items.title: Routers Are a New AI Primitive (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google Quantum AI has demonstrated that 'magic state cultivation' works in practice on its Willow processor. Magic states help researchers create the operations they need for going beyond classical computing. Creating high-quality, error-corrected magic states is incredibly resource-heavy. This post details how Google Quantum AI created a magic state cultivation protocol that achieved a 40-fold reduction in errors. The breakthrough is a crucial step towards scaling up quantum computing to practical use.
items.title: Bringing the magic: Google breaks open a bottleneck in quantum computing (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Training an AI model fundamentally requires lots and lots of examples of something being done correctly. Creating this data for training robots is expensive, and companies need a lot of data to train competent models. Large language models showed the benefits of scale when training models. Researchers are now working hard to gather enormous amounts of robot task training data in the hopes of seeing the same sort of trends with robotic capabilities.

items.summary_html: Developers are using Claude to debug hardware issues. This convinced much of the field that networks pack concepts arbitrarily, but what looked like arbitrary packing was mostly recursive generalization, which is less concerning. This means networks can be studied directly, instead of needing to be untangled first. The outlook for mechanistic interpretability may be far better than we thought.

items.summary_html: Reinforcement learning, on-policy distillation, and supervised fine-tuning on near-policy data change only a small fraction of parameters. Small and sparse are different claims. The expected gradient is a covariance, the Fisher is a variance, and the Fisher caps the gradient for any reward. At one position, the Fisher is the variance of logit sensitivities: whatever moves every candidate together counts for nothing. None of this needs on-policy sampling - it needs a score centered under the sampling distribution.
items.title: The Gradient Is a Covariance (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Doing reinforcement learning for agent use-cases is conceptually not at all that complicated. For each problem, you set up a VM with a harness and a fresh model context, send the prompt, let the model make tool calls, score the whole thing at the end, and update the weights. Agentic post-training means there's more than the model to consider. Even when the harness is consistent, you can still go off-policy with the trajectories themselves. Agents spawn subagents, make parallel tool calls, and compact large sessions, which adds complexity.

items.summary_html: Google ran magic state cultivation on its Willow chip, cutting errors about 40x versus uncultivated states and reaching a record 99.99% logical fidelity for T-states. Magic states are a bottleneck because making them could consume up to 95% of a quantum computer's capacity. Cultivation injects a noisy state into a small chip region, then uses coordinated measurements to discard flawed attempts, and Google grafted a distance-3 color code onto a distance-5 surface code. Larger-scale demonstrations are still needed.
items.title: Google's Willow chip cuts quantum magic-state errors 40x with cultivation (4 minute read)

Several projects are now working to ensure formal libraries fulfill the community's mathematical goals. Within the next few years, most of mathematics will be able to be formalized in such a way that mathematicians can explore, build on, and make use of formal libraries. This will significantly extend their ability to develop and discover new mathematics.
items.title: How to Formalize All of Mathematics (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Decoherence is the accumulation of locally valid but mutually incompatible or redundant models within a system. It causes the cost of change to be dominated by translating among those models and preventing unintended side-effects. Decoherence grows relative to the rate of change of a system, and it increases faster the more decoherent a system is, resulting in runaway exponential growth. It rules out the specter of runaway recursive self-improvement, as decoherence both prevents AI from improving in a bubble and limits the rate at which it can improve outside of it. However, it also introduces a new kind of disaster called Decoherence Collapse.
items.title: Decoherence (48 minute read)

However, it could also lead to independent human scientific activity progressively weakening, the production of new knowledge becoming increasingly concentrated in a small number of hands, and knowledge becoming alien to human understanding. The future will likely be a combination of these scenarios.
items.title: Will it be a golden age or a dark age for mathematics (and science)? (23 minute read)

items.summary_html: Gittifacts routes agent-written changes to auto-merge, quick review, or full review based on test evidence and repository policy, after a human approves the plan. Missing signals can only increase scrutiny, and feature flags make merged changes reversible. Auto-merge still relies on the submitting agent's test environment for some evidence, while evidence generation took 13 to 17 minutes per change on the project's own repository.
items.title: Humans approve intent, machines prove conformance (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: HybridAgent is a research approach for training AI agents to reason internally using numerical representations instead of writing out every intermediate thought, while still producing text to call tools such as Python or web search and deliver answers. In tests, a 14B Qwen3 model trained this way scored 52.4 on GAIA versus 43.7 for a matched text-only agent, with estimated decoding costs falling from $470 to $176 per million questions.
items.title: HybridAgent Thinks in Latent Space and Acts in Text (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: AWS Lambda Web Functions run standard Node.js HTTP servers without adapters, with each execution environment handling concurrent requests and streaming responses. In a sample run of 300 streaming requests with up to 200 open at once, five environments consumed 4.75 seconds of CPU. Billing covers active CPU, memory, and requests, so waiting on a database or API uses little CPU but still incurs other charges.
items.title: Exploring AWS Lambda Web Functions for building web applications (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Good products reflect a shared point of view shaped by experience, customer conversations, and judgment. When teams use agents to add features independently, individually useful changes can weaken the product's coherence unless someone keeps shaping the whole.
items.title: Someone Behind the Software (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Elegant systems often gain simplicity and scale by accepting limits on freshness, coordination, or flexibility. Coding agents tend to invent extra requirements, so explicitly stating which compromises are acceptable can prevent unnecessary locks, checks, and layers of abstraction.
items.title: What Requirements Don't You Have? (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Frameworks remain useful when agents write the code because they supply structure, shared maintenance, and familiar abstractions. Rewriting an application in a faster language can change behavior that users rely on, making targeted optimization and dependency updates a more practical starting point. Familiar code also makes it easier to review the decisions an agent makes.
items.title: Does Ruby on Rails Still Make Sense? (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs give agents and RAG applications live search results and web pages converted to Markdown. Both use standard DeepSeek API keys and cost $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests, with empty results, failures, and timeouts excluded from billing.
items.title: DeepSeek Search & Fetch (Website)

items.summary_html: Sphinx pauses pushes to protected branches and quizzes developers on what agent-written code does, including failure scenarios. A separate reviewer reads the diff without seeing the development chat, explains incorrect answers, and asks a new scenario before allowing the push. It supports existing coding agents and configurable model endpoints, with a logged bypass for skipped checks.
items.title: Sphinx (Website)

items.summary_html: Rakazo is an open-source, self-hosted AI assistant for running persistent bots with their own memory, routines, and conversations. Bots can use browsers, terminals, files, and desktop interfaces, with your choice of model and local or hosted computer environments. The project is in beta and offers web, desktop, and mobile clients.
items.title: Rakazo (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: An internal Claude research model traced the seeds of five NIST prime curves to the lrand48 random-number generator initialized with Unix timestamps, explaining a decades-old provenance mystery. Anthropic says the findings strengthen confidence in the curves and do not reveal a cryptographic break. Some base-point origins, skipped candidates, and one binary-curve seed remain unexplained.
items.title: Claude Reveals ECDSA Curve Origins (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: In a comparison run once per model, Gemini 4 Argon matched Claude Opus 5.5 on finding and fixing 14 planted bugs at lower cost, but performed worse on billing and long-context dependency tasks. One incorrect API call caused most billing failures, and a manual one-line fix brought Argon to full marks. Its long-context answers still missed or invented dependencies, showing why the results need to be read beyond the headline scores.
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon vs. Claude Opus 5.5 (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs give agents and RAG applications access to live web content. The Search API finds web pages for a query and returns structured results. items.summary_html: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 delivers substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. It also reduces task execution time and output length, advancing the performance-cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer KV cache reuse in Compressed Sparse Attention 2 with FP4 KV caching, reducing its global KV cache footprint to 890 bytes per token. Its persistent KV cache footprint is roughly 1/8 of that of DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The model delivers substantially better performance than the baseline despite its much smaller KV cache footprint.
items.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (Hugging Face Repo)

items.title: How the Claude Code team does code review (18 minute read)

It credits AI-driven DRAM shortages, expanded capacity, and more output per wafer. items.title: CXMT swings to a nearly $20B nine-month profit as AI demand drives up DRAM prices (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: After moving Roman's secondary mirror by about one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, engineers measured 63 nanometers RMS of optical error in the Wide Field Instrument, nearly 30% better than the 90-nanometer requirement. The camera has 18 detectors, and the same adjustment fixed slight defocus in the Coronagraph Instrument, which still needs testing of its ability to block unwanted light. Roman launched August 30, and both instruments now match or beat predictions.
items.title: NASA's Roman telescope beats its image-quality spec by nearly 30% after a hair-width mirror nudge (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Roadster's floor uses fans and perimeter seals to pull air out from under the car, creating up to 2 g of suction, enough to hold it upside down while stationary, and at speed, front and rear passages open for more flow. Cold-gas thrusters add a second system: ten nozzles fed by compressed air, with all-electric actuators for fast micro-adjustments, which Tesla says push with four to five times the force tires can deliver.
items.title: Tesla Roadster pairs underbody suction fans with cold-gas thrusters for grip beyond what tires allow (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Variable frequency drives adjust motor speed to match demand, cutting a motor's energy use by about 40 to 60 percent. Toyota saved over $700,000 a year after putting them on 200-plus HVAC motors at its Kentucky plant, in a $1.25 million pilot. Cheaper sensors, machine-learning control, and power chips borrowed from EVs and solar inverters have cut costs. ABB claims drives on every motor could cover up to five years of data center load growth.
items.title: Variable frequency drives could free up grid power by cutting motor energy use 40 to 60 percent (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Argonne and UIUC researchers coupled spin waves in a thin yttrium iron garnet film to a superconducting resonator built directly on top, creating a hybrid mode that propagates one way and could keep return noise from leaking back into qubits. The key materials fix was swapping the usual rare-earth-containing substrate, which absorbs microwaves at low temperatures, for one without rare-earth metals. It's still a proof of concept.
items.title: Spin waves coupled to a superconducting circuit create a one-way street for microwave signals (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Kornia-SLAM is an open-source visual-inertial odometry and spatial mapping library implemented entirely in Rust. It supports monocular, stereo, and RGB-D cameras coupled with inertial measurement units, utilizing factor graph optimization to maintain real-time performance and strict memory safety. This framework gives embedded software teams a reliable, crash-resilient foundation for real-time spatial estimation on compute-limited physical devices.
items.title: Kornia-SLAM: Visual-Inertial Odometry and SLAM in Rust (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 4 Argon, a multimodal foundation model engineered specifically for embodied physical systems. Featuring native spatio-temporal reasoning and low-latency action generation, it links high-level semantic understanding directly to robot execution through native bridges for ROS 2 and physics simulators like MuJoCo. The architecture allows creators of intelligent physical machines to translate natural language goals into dexterous, real-world manipulation and navigation.
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Multimodal Foundation Models for Embodied Intelligence (4 minute read)

items.title: AMD shows how to hand-tune an FP16 GEMM kernel on RDNA 3 and RDNA 4 to match hipBLASLt (25 minute read)

items.summary_html: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis is a weaker version of the Riemann hypothesis, arguably the biggest open question in math. Resolving the Riemann hypothesis would enable mathematicians to better understand the nature of prime numbers. OpenAI's recently released proof for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis is the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far, by quite a margin. The vast majority of the consequences of resolving it already follow from solving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now? (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Endurance Energy, a Seattle-based startup, recently demonstrated the technical feasibility of using an active underwater volcano to generate electricity. The startup deployed a 3-ton prototype power plant at the Axial Seamount in the northeast Pacific Ocean in September and generated less than 10 seconds of net-positive electricity. The company's next trial run, planned for the winter of 2026 to 2027, will aim to sustain higher power generation. It is currently developing a 2-megawatt commercial generator for its first planned commercial deployment with the Kingdom of Tonga in 2027.
items.title: Startup taps underwater volcano as energy source in “proof point” test (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Clairic is an extraction model. Extraction models are a new class of System One-style models that can extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs, all at significantly higher accuracy, faster latency, and lower cost than traditional LLMs. It answers with values directly extracted from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it. The model can't produce a mistyped answer or hallucinate in the same way an LLM can, but it can still make mistakes.
items.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cloudflare lowered its average review cost from $2.43 to $0.77. The biggest single saving came from checking what actually reached the provider on each session's first request, and finding a way to order those messages in a way that was as consistent as possible across commits, merge requests, and repositories. Check whether each session's first request actually reads from the cache and whether reviewers still find real problems at the effort level being paid for.
items.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Some worry about radiology being totally automated, but the more likely outcome is a future where there is more demand for services as predictive power increases. This is similar to how programming is thriving despite drastic change in the field. It may be possible one day to use radiology images to predict disease probabilities far into the future. Any domain where demand can be elastic and quality can scale with increased intelligence will similarly flourish with the development of AI.
items.title: AI will not automate radiologists like you think (6 minute read)

items.title: No more tech debt (4 minute read)

Privacy increasingly depends on who can stop collection. AI assistants and paid privacy tiers will make that question more pressing.
items.title: Who Holds the Off Switch? (24 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude Duet is a proactive agent that delivers morning briefs, handles tasks while you are away, and asks for approval when needed. The research preview uses Opus 5.5, carries over Claude memory, skills, and apps, and is offered through a waitlist for US Pro and Max users.
items.title: Claude Duet (Website)

items.summary_html: Omnara is an open-source managed agent platform that can run with different model providers and execute tools on sandboxes or your own machines. A REST API, TypeScript SDK, CLI, and dashboard expose agent runs, while a Postgres event log lets workers resume them after crashes.
items.title: Omnara (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Slower transistor scaling, memory bottlenecks, and power limits are renewing the case for specialized AI inference hardware. Matching different inference phases to different accelerators can improve performance per watt while adding deployment and software complexity and leaving room for GPUs to absorb successful ideas.
items.title: Why Hardware Specialization Is Back (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's Jalapeño inference chip links 64 dedicated cores to individual HBM memory banks to reduce data movement and improve utilization. This interview explains the tradeoff in memory-management complexity, the choice to keep prefill and decode on fungible hardware, and how AI-assisted optimization accelerated chip design and kernel development.
items.title: Inside OpenAI's Jalapeño AI Chip (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Reliable evaluation of open-ended agent tasks combines calibrated human judgments, automated judges or rubrics, and production monitoring. Power analysis, confidence intervals, and repeated runs help distinguish improvements from noise, while realistic, diverse tasks, and production feedback keep benchmarks useful.
items.title: Evaluating Agents on Highly Subjective Tasks (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI frontier models and Codex workflows are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden.
items.title: OpenAI Models Are Coming to Google Cloud (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Railway reports possible unauthorized access to customer environment variables, including some decrypted contents, and recommends rotating stored secrets and private registry credentials while reviewing service logs.
items.title: Railway Security Disclosure (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google's Rust style guide covers code organization, formatting, ownership, API design, traits, errors, and concurrency.
items.title: Google Rust Style Guide (Website)

items.summary_html: Narrating your reasoning aloud can aid problem-solving by exposing assumptions, organizing dependencies, making rules explicit, and clarifying choices for backtracking.
items.title: Chain of Thought for Humans (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent powered by Opus 5.5 that monitors connected apps, prioritizes tasks, and works autonomously while requesting approval before certain actions. The research preview initially targeted US Pro and Max subscribers through a waitlist.
items.title: Claude Duet (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Recursive Flint is a mixture-of-experts model built for fast agentic coding on local hardware. It has 40 billion total parameters but activates just 2.5 billion per token. It was built from scratch by a small team of people and agents in under four months. Flint generates more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and more than 150 tokens per second on a 64GB NVIDIA RTX Spark at short contexts. It can be used as a daily coding model to complete tasks locally without sending data to a remote server.
items.title: Introducing Flint (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's frontier models and Codex agentic workflows are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden. The integration will give customers native access to these models to power complex agentic workflows at scale. It will pair OpenAI's frontier models with Google Cloud's built-in access controls, centralized data governance, and high-performance infrastructure to support demanding enterprise workloads. OpenAI models will soon be available in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent.
items.title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Long Lake argues that acquiring established service businesses solves AI deployment barriers through customer trust, expert knowledge, proprietary data, and aligned incentives. Backed by $7.5B, the company has partnered with 40 businesses to turn automation into measurable operating gains.
items.title: If Intelligence Is Getting Cheap, What Remains Expensive? (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude Mods flips the agent harness paradigm to face the human, creating a customizable "Attention Interface" for Claude AI. Mods are TypeScript or JavaScript functions that alter Claude Code's behavior in real-time, allowing users to design how Claude interacts with them. This shift lets users program the human-agent interface and even have Claude build mods, enhancing workflow and decision-making.
items.title: Claude Mods: Flipping the Harness Inside Out (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Language models can encode messages in images. These messages can be decoded by the same language model even if no information about the encoding method is passed. The act of decoding the hidden messages is obvious if the tool calls of the decoding model are monitored. The encoded messaging is surprisingly hard to spot, and it could be used as a precursor to steganography in images.
items.title: How does Fable 5.1 hide messages in images? (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Mammoth-1 and Elephant-1, decision models from Base Labs, top benchmarks like the Jev Decision Index and Artificial Analysis Decision Index.
items.title: Mammoth-1 and Elephant-1: frontier decision models (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Claude API has received its first official version release since 2023. Anthropic plans to release versions more often so developers can handle breaking changes before a new model requires them. 2023-06-10 is not deprecated. New major versions of the Anthropic SDKs and CLI are out today and default to the new API. A migration guide is available.
items.title: Claude API version 2026-10-21 is now available (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Humming is a general-purpose kernel library for quantized inference. It features broad device support, extensive quantization support, and strong execution performance. Humming's unified architecture makes it straightforward to tune execution parameters and collect pipelines for different workloads.
items.title: Announcing Humming: Fast, Flexible Kernels for Quantized Inference (19 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI coordinated with PHP maintainers and security partners to patch critical vulnerabilities discovered using GPT-5.6 Sol and independently by Wiz. The company also released a PHP vulnerability checker and proposed a framework for coordinating responses to AI-discovered security flaws.
items.title: OpenAI's PHP Patcher (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Peter Steinberger, the creator of OpenClaw and now a member of technical staff at OpenAI, estimates that he spent around $10 million in tokens running AI workloads last month, all from out of investors' pockets. Steinberger has a virtually unlimited token budget, allowing him to work differently from others in the industry. This article collects some of his answers during a conversation with Cloudflare's CTO at the Cloudflare Connect 2026 conference.
items.title: OpenClaw creator says he spent $10 million in tokens last month (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A malicious LiteLLM package was published to PyPI and was live for approximately 2 hours before it was pulled.
items.title: Contained: Oct 21, 2026 LiteLLM release v1.107.0 Compromised (11 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI CLI (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Agent Matrix is a platform that coordinates multiple AI agents working continuously toward revenue growth.
items.title: Monaco Launches Agent Matrix for Revenue Growth (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: GUI-Owl 1.5 is a 2-billion-parameter screen model that can read an Android screen through the accessibility service and tap and type in any other app.
items.title: Computer use on the phone itself: a 2B model that operates Android apps (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Dario Amodei responds to a post regarding Anthropic's stance on AI safety by listing the things that the company did in the past year that were pro-safety and commercially costly to it.
items.title: A response from Dario Amodei (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Three OpenAI safety researchers were fired after security officers discovered Signal chats with disappearing messages turned on on their personal devices. OpenAI claimed the researchers were fired for violating clear policies for handling sensitive information and not for raising safety concerns or speaking out. The researchers had spent recent months at the company pushing for more industry collaboration on safety. They claim their firings will serve as an excuse for OpenAI to close a channel to independent third-party insight.
items.title: The Signal Chats That Cost OpenAI Researchers Their Jobs (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Alexa Tablet lineup offers a more open approach to software than Amazon's previous Fire brand that lets consumers use the devices like any other Android tablet. Users can download apps from the Google Play Store and access popular services like Gmail and YouTube. Amazon previously restricted access to its own app marketplace. The 12-inch Alexa Tablet Pro is well constructed and has a smooth 12-hertz display, making it competitive with Apple's iPads.
items.title: Amazon's New Tablet Is a Credible iPad Rival for Much Less Money (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX is in talks with Crown Castle Inc., one of the largest owners of cellular towers in the US, as part of its plans to secure a minimum of 80,000 cell sites across the country. Crown Castle is likely also in talks with Amazon and other satellite-based telecom providers regarding leasing deals. Elon Musk has openly discussed creating a standalone wireless carrier from scratch. SpaceX recently acquired low-band spectrum and has received approval to launch 15,000 satellites to provide mobile service directly to phones.
items.title: SpaceX in Talks to Access 80,000 Cell Sites for New Network (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Moderna and Merck's personalized mRNA vaccines against melanoma demonstrate how mRNA technology has the potential to fundamentally challenge how cancer is treated. The vaccine's success offers a new paradigm for cancer therapies. The companies are already engaging with regulatory authorities to get the vaccine approved.
items.title: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42% (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: We need ways to prove that code is free from bugs. Formal software verification, which could provide this guarantee, has always required years of expert effort, but LLMs can now produce formal proofs at large scale. This enables new software development workflows that include proven security guarantees. Formal verification will likely become an essential part of secure software development as model capabilities continue to improve.
items.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale (23 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic employs around 3,500 staff, but its coding output is closer to that of a company with 35,000 to 70,000 staff. Big tech companies like Google and Meta moved off Git a long time ago because it did not scale for them. Both built their own custom solutions, just like Anthropic did with Scion. This post provides some details about how Anthropic's custom source control system works.
items.title: Anthropic builds its own source control system (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Mathematics seems to be a field where the outputs are celebrated less as examples of subjective expression and more as advancements in knowledge and understanding. A mathematician's work may be informed by their experience, but that's not what gives their contributions value. Mathematical knowledge remains objectively true whether it is observed by humans or sea sponges or computer programs.
items.title: An artist's take on AI in math (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ondřej Surý is one of the volunteers who helps maintain and automate patches for PHP. He alone is responsible for most of the world's distribution of PHP. His work, along with just a handful of others, has allowed countless websites and organizations to fix the recently revealed PHP vulnerabilities quickly. He's become arguably the unsung hero of the entire internet, despite the fact that the only compensation he receives for his work is from donations. This article features an interview with Surý where he discusses the unfolding AI-cybersecurity crisis, how the internet's infrastructure is maintained by small crews of volunteers, and how it feels to save the web.
items.title: ‘If Anything Happens to This Guy … Everyone Is Screwed' (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Most programs can't be meaningfully sped up by rewriting them in C or Rust.
items.title: Software is slow because of bad design, not slow languages (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: The US has become increasingly reliant on foreign nations for dogs that play an important role in the US military and law enforcement.
items.title: Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Supervisory engineering work is a different job from software engineering and so requires a different system around it.
items.title: Supervisory Engineering Work (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Finance companies in the AI era need to be built around continuous decisions, portable assets, and delegated distribution.
items.title: Finance in the intelligence era (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: We are the ones who get to decide what to do with all of the productivity that AI creates.
items.title: I'm not doing 996 (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: JPEG XL is the end-game universal image format because it has excellent compression efficiency, a universal feature set, wide color depth, gamut, and native HDR, lossless JPEG transcoding, high-speed parallel software encoding and decoding, and an open-source, permissive license.
items.title: JPEG XL, Welcome to the Web! (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Folding routers, planners, and domain specialists into a single agent loop can reduce lossy handoffs, cost, and latency when skills and tool search load context on demand. Anthropic describes migration patterns and evaluations for deciding which boundaries to remove. Separate agents still help with independent parallel work, verification, permission boundaries, and measurable context overload.
items.title: Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic replaced Git in its monorepo with Scion as daily merges grew from about 2,500 to more than 30,000 and CI reached 25 million checkouts a day. Its Rust client and server store changesets in Spanner and blobs in Google Cloud Storage, with a separate review system replacing GitHub's workflow.
items.title: Anthropic builds its own source control system (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Stream's incident agent gathers logs, metrics, database results, and code references, then has a fresh session challenge its conclusions before posting findings. Read-only tools, isolated credentials, restricted networking, and output filters enforce its limits outside the prompt. Engineers approve every fix, while 22 evaluation cases test real incidents and past mistakes.
items.title: We Built an AI Agent to Investigate Production Issues (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Building a container runtime exposes Docker as a collection of Linux mechanisms, including namespaces, cgroups, and filesystem isolation around ordinary processes. This walkthrough explains why Go's multithreaded runtime complicates container setup and why rootless networking often requires extra work in userspace.
items.title: Docker is weird (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Imprint is testing a faster review path for narrowly scoped changes as rising PR volume pushes median review time from 33 to 77 minutes. Eligibility depends on a CI-controlled check covering change size, service experience, scope, and automated review findings, with shared libraries and sensitive paths excluded. Errors are treated as failures to improve in the verification system.
items.title: Speeding up code review with small-change (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI adoption needs changes to incentives, working practices, and support alongside software licenses. Staff need role-specific training, time to experiment, and a reason to share in productivity gains without fearing punishment for mistakes. Shadow AI can reveal gaps in official tools that blanket restrictions only push out of sight.
items.title: Is Your Organization Messing Up AI Adoption? (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: TanStack AI brings 76 packages to stable APIs for chat, tools, media, MCP, persistence, and sandboxes while preserving provider and framework choice. Upgrade all client and server packages together and replace APIs deprecated in 0.x. The newly introduced agent harness remains experimental.
items.title: TanStack AI 1.0: Still Your AI, Still Your Way (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenShell runs agents in policy-controlled sandboxes with kernel-enforced file and network limits, credential injection, and formal checks on proposed access changes.
items.title: NVIDIA OpenShell (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: ns2jb is a software-only, tethered jailbreak demonstrated on Switch 2 firmware 23.0.1. It enables native code execution for homebrew and game modifications.
items.title: Jailbreaking the Switch 2 (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI21 combined a switch to DeepSeek V4 Flash with context compaction to cut GitLab Duo Code Review's estimated token cost from $0.589 to $0.0135 per pull request on a public benchmark, with F1 rising from 46.4% to 47.2%. Compaction made oversized reviews fit the deployment's context window, removing expensive fallbacks to Sonnet.
items.title: How we cut GitLab Duo Code Review's cost by 98% (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Public Suffix List records the boundaries browsers and password managers need to distinguish independently controlled sites on shared domains. Its rules prevent cookies and saved credentials from crossing tenant boundaries, but growing demand leaves volunteers reviewing increasingly complex submissions. The article explains why DNS has not replaced the list and why using it for unrelated controls can create problems.
items.title: What the heck is the Public Suffix List? (21 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude produced machine-checked proofs for 239 fuzz-test entry points across 123 open-source libraries, turning existing tests into specifications over compiled RISC-V code. The guarantees cover inputs below 64 MB under a single-threaded Linux model with fixed memory limits, so they establish specific security properties rather than complete program correctness.
items.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Making a screen's relevant state explicit lets people and agents inspect combinations of roles, plans, billing states, and feature flags before merging a change.
items.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: 1Password lets users approve sign-ins for supported agents and fills credentials into destination sites without exposing passwords to the model.
items.title: Introducing 1Password for Agents (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: TypeUI offers 113 interactive examples for buttons, forms, modals, navigation, and other UI patterns.
items.title: TypeUI Micro Interactions (Website)
