items.title: State of HTML 2026 (Website)

items.summary_html: OpenAI is closing in on a funding round that could value it at more than $1 trillion. Investors from the United Arab Emirates are leading the round. The round is being positioned as an opportunistic bridge ahead of a potential IPO. OpenAI is aiming to secure signatures by the end of next week, but the final size of the round is still being determined.
items.title: OpenAI nears up to $30 billion funding round at $1.25 trillion valuation led by UAE investors (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: 1Password introduced a platform that lets AI agents authenticate to websites without accessing users' passwords directly. Agents can request credentials from a user's vault, and once approved, 1Password autofills them into the destination site while keeping the credentials hidden from the agent.
items.title: Introducing 1Password for Agents (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: WorldTUI is a 360-million-parameter model fine-tuned to act as a terminal. The model predicts how the screen will change for every key press, and there is no shell or file system behind it. WorldTUI can create files, run vim and tmux, play snake, and usually remember commands. It can repair mistakes and decode screen rows in parallel. A browser demo is available.
items.title: WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: A unilateral US pause will fail because rivals would catch up within about a year, so any slowdown needs a treaty that catches defection early. This post surveys how one could govern compute through remote sensing, on-site inspections, and hardware mechanisms like chip licensing and location verification.
items.title: How the US and China Could Verifiably Slow AI (29 minute read)

items.summary_html: METR and Redwood Research conducted a three-week security assessment with access to OpenAI's internal infrastructure, identifying vulnerabilities that could allow AI agents to evade monitoring, bypass sandbox restrictions, or conceal actions.
items.title: How Researchers Tested OpenAI's Internal Agent Monitoring (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Flapping Airplanes' potential valuation jump from $1.5B to $5B may reflect investor hype rather than verified technical progress. Breakthroughs in sample-efficient AI could accelerate superintelligence timelines and make compute-based treaty enforcement harder.
items.title: Does Flapping Airplanes Mean Short Timelines and Hard Treaty Enforcement? (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's latest Claude models embed a SynthID-Text-based watermark in all text output to comply with the EU AI Act. It works by nudging choices among near-equivalent words, adds no hidden characters or tokens, and carries no information about the user.
items.title: Claude's Text Output Now Carries an Invisible Watermark (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Perplexity's JOLT is a self-distillation method that jointly trains a model as both teacher and student, adapting feedback to the student's capabilities. It improved performance and training efficiency across mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks.
items.title: A Novel Self-Distillation Method (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: A single Cerebras WSE-3T wafer has 44 GB of on-chip memory. Trillion-parameter frontier models need terabytes of memory for their weights alone. This post explains how the company splits a large frontier model across multiple WSE-3T wafers. It covers how models are filled into on-chip memory, how models are mapped across multiple chips, and how Cerebras handles a high number of concurrent requests.
items.title: How we deploy Trillion-parameter frontier models on Cerebras (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA has introduced Joints, Camera, Action! (JCA), a system that generates videos and synchronized 3D motion for arbitrary character rigs from text prompts. It supports scene-aware motion, keyframe-based control, and bidirectional conversion between video and rig animation.
items.title: NVIDIA's Video Generation with Matching 3D Motion (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's Jalapeño AI inference chip outperforms its rivals in performance per watt. It is likely the most promising chip program in the latest wave of non-GPU AI chips. This post contains highlights from a conversation with one of the top engineers in the AI and chip industry. The interview is packed with technical details and insights on where chip design and memory technology are going.
items.title: An Interview with OpenAI's Richard Ho on Why Jalapeño Is a Groundbreaking AI Chip (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google had both Flash and Pro versions of the 3.5 series. However, there were gaps in the model's agentic capabilities, particularly around coding. The team felt the fastest way to climb that hill was to use Flash, as the smaller model allowed for more iterative loops. By the time the team had improved Flash's abilities, Argon pre-training was done.
items.title: What happened to the missing Gemini 3.5 Pro model that never shipped? (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude Platform features are now available on Google Cloud with Google Cloud authentication, billing, and commitment retirement.
items.title: The full Claude Platform, available on Google Cloud (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft launched the Microsoft-Decision-1 model, focusing on scoring predefined answer options with confidence probabilities rather than generating text.
items.title: Microsoft Decision-1: 9B Qwen Model Launch Explained (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic donated its Agent Skills open standard to the Agentic AI Foundation, placing its development under vendor-neutral governance.
items.title: Anthropic Donates Agent Skills to Linux Foundation (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Dwarkesh Patel toured Intel's fabs and interviewed its leaders. CTO Pushkar Ranade said that there are enough tools to roughly double leading-edge output, not 10x. Backside power lets Intel's 14A print with a single High-NA pass, where TSMC would still need double-patterned EUV. Other topics discussed included ruthenium wiring below roughly 20nm pitch, CFET aspect-ratio and heat challenges, hybrid bonding pitches shrinking toward 0.45 microns, and the Terafab partnership.
items.title: Intel's CTO says tools can only roughly double leading-edge chip output, while AI demand grows 3x a year (50 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agility Robotics will use Nvidia's IGX Thor modules as the exclusive onboard computer for the general-sale version of Digit 5, with early access starting in the first half of 2027. The robot also adopts parts of Nvidia's Halos safety platform, whose inspection lab will check Digit's safety software before outside certification. Agility reports more than $300 million in multi-year Digit 5 orders, four new customers, and a new Pittsburgh site, as it prepares to list on Nasdaq via a merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI.
items.title: Agility's Digit 5 humanoid robot will run on Nvidia as it heads for Nasdaq (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Brookhaven National Laboratory debuted a superconducting chip built with other US Department of Energy facilities and AI hardware startup Great Sky to monitor fusion plasma in real time. The chip runs a neuromorphic neural network meant to spot signs that superhot plasma is about to become unstable. Its backers hope the hardware is fast enough to help control plasma before disruptions form, a prerequisite for practical fusion power.
items.title: New superconducting chip aims to help tame fusion plasma (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Regent's Viceroy Seaglider, the largest electric wing-in-ground-effect craft to fly with people aboard, made its maiden flight on September 2, covering 596 meters over 30 seconds at about 10 meters above the water. The 16.8-meter craft carries 12 passengers at up to 290 kph with a 290-kilometer range, and is classified as a maritime vessel under US law, sidestepping the FAA certification limbo facing eVTOLs. Regent has raised more than $340 million, claims a $10 billion order backlog, and plans commercial production at the end of 2027.
items.title: Electric Seagliders Promise Faster Coastal Travel by 2028 (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Commerce Department plans four awards: up to $175 million for Helion's high-voltage power semiconductors and modules for fusion, $85 million for Commonwealth Fusion Systems' plasma-heating and radiation-hardened electronics, and $73 million for Vertical Semiconductor's vertical gallium nitride devices for AI racks. Sibelco gets $56 million for ultra-high-purity quartz purification.
items.title: Commerce plans $389M for power semiconductors, with the government taking equity stakes (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 enables real-time, interactive world simulations through models like Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual, -Transfer, and -Auto. These models support action-conditioned dynamics, spatial control for high-quality visual outputs, and synchronized multi-view video for tasks like autonomous driving. Leveraging advanced spatial and language controls, the models surpass performance benchmarks in depth, edge, and video quality metrics.
items.title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The $1,999 iPhone Duo has reached its first customers in Australia and New Zealand, with rollout moving through Asia, the Middle East, Europe, then North America. Early owners praise the matte 7.6-inch inner display and a nearly invisible crease, and note the under-screen camera is occasionally visible, with Touch ID in place of Face ID. Apple expects stock to sell out on launch day, and online shipping estimates have slipped to January 25.
items.title: Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo foldable reaches its first customers with stock already tight (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX recorded a $561 million non-cash gain in Q3 from its minority stake in The Boring Co., more than half of its "other income," lifting net income to just over $4 billion. The mark-up follows Boring Co.'s $3 billion raise last month at a $23 billion valuation, backed by UAE investors. Boring Co. started inside SpaceX in 2017 and was spun out a year later.
items.title: SpaceX books a $561M unrealized gain on its Boring Co. stake (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: KAIST researchers developed a method to predict blue OLED lifetimes by measuring tiny brightness changes under magnetic fields.
items.title: Magnetic Field Tests Predict Blue OLED Lifetimes (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX's $40 billion raise, led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, is pricing at about 8.3% on the lowest-rated tranche, while a safer piece backed by some of its chips is expected near 7.75%.
items.title: SpaceX's $40B chip-financing debt prices at up to 8.3% as AI fears spread (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Oura sued Ultrahuman again, alleging the redesigned Ring Pro infringes two patents on the ring's design and internals, including a curved battery, circuit board, magnets, and sensors.
items.title: Oura sues Ultrahuman again over the redesigned Ring Pro's internals (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: High-frequency traders are now racing for compute. They are investing in the sector as it secures them access to greater processing capacity and faster chips. These firms primarily profit from tiny price differences as they move rapidly in and out of positions. As they increasingly rely on machine learning, their success is directly tied to their computing power. While the risks are significant, most high-speed traders see few options if they want to avoid becoming obsolete.
items.title: Jane Street and Rivals Are Now Fighting for AI Power as Well as Pace (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple's iPhone Duo is a miniature tablet that can be folded up into a phone. Its main target audience is people who want to have a tablet everywhere they go. Commuters and business travelers who spend a lot of time on trains, buses, and planes will probably like the device. Everyone else may feel frustrated with what is otherwise an average smartphone.
items.title: Review of iPhone Duo: A New Chapter That Redefines a Smartphone's Purpose (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Researchers have developed an implantable neural chip that tracks communication across brain regions. It can record brain activity and extract biomarkers that describe the strength of brain waves and synchrony between signals from different brain regions. These signals can be decoded using a machine-learning algorithm to distinguish between cognitive and emotional states. The capability to extract brain-network biomarkers to trigger precisely timed stimulation has many applications across next-generation neurotechnology.
items.title: Neural chip decodes interactions between brain regions (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX has been granted access to restricted space tracking data by the US military. The access raises new national security questions as well as questions about whether the Trump administration is attempting to hand over traffic control in Earth's orbit to a donor. Elon Musk's Doge program fired many of the federal government's space traffic control staff in 2025, and the administration has twice attempted to financially gut the Traffic Coordination System for Space department. The moves have been widely viewed in the industry as an attempt by Musk to privatize space traffic control.
items.title: US military gives Elon Musk's SpaceX access to sensitive tracking data (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Context engineering is hard in unique ways because AI models aren't people. It helps to understand how models are built, optimized, and trained. Their unique attributes and construction create a unique set of failure modes to be reckoned with. This means context engineering will forever be a challenge with AI, no matter how good it gets.
items.title: The State of Context Engineering (21 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI can now one-shot many projects, allowing almost anyone to create software. However, it still struggles with many harder tasks. People who say that everything just works or that software is solved aren't working on the hard problems. They need to be more ambitious about the software they're building as AI models become more capable.
items.title: We should be more ambitious with the software we build (37 minute read)

items.summary_html: This post tells the story of what it was like at Salesforce after it acquired Slack. The cultural gaps between the two companies were evident. Slack had a tight-knit culture where humans would help each other, whereas Salesforce was a much larger company with systems and processes for things to get done. Slack's cognitive overhead was nothing compared to the overbearing weight of the Salesforce monolith.
items.title: Salesforce – Part Two (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: TSMC Arizona's first plant has been producing chips for two years. Its rate of output in Phoenix is comparable to that in Taiwan. TSMC sends engineers to Arizona on contracts of up to three years, with families moving from Taiwan to the site. Some of the families that moved in the first wave now want to build lives in the US, as they want to give their children a chance to integrate, for their kids' education, or because they prefer the American lifestyle, and there are legal pathways for doing so. This article looks at the impact the factory had on Phoenix, the employees who moved to America to work there, and the chip manufacturing industry in the US.
items.title: The Factory in Phoenix That Could Save American Manufacturing (28 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cap 0.6.1 is the first version that doesn't have a web browser inside it.
items.title: A technical deep dive into Cap's migration to GPUI (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Jev hype cycle is a prime example of the manipulative marketing that we are all too familiar with at this point.
items.title: The rise and fall of Jev hype (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: We are trying really hard to make agents productive while we're not around, but that requires excellent planning.
items.title: Planning with Agents: Divided Worlds, Boundary Objects, and Thicker Interfaces (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Most people will no longer need to be significant producers of intelligence in order to become significant consumers of it.
items.title: Cognitive Mercantilism (23 minute read)

items.summary_html: It's strange that OpenAI and Anthropic cut their primary revenue sources at a time when they are losing billions and are planning to IPO soon.
items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut their LLM prices by up to 80% within a few months. Why? (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: We have to direct our attention more consciously as the future hinges on the choices we make now.
items.title: Attention is All You Need (26 minute read)

items.summary_html: Dropbox routes user edits, automated scheduling, and agent actions through one shared Schedule Action type so they use the same validation logic. Preview Mode makes proposed changes reviewable, backed by a scheduler refactored into a pure function and accelerated with Redis.
items.title: Reclaim goes AI-native without starting over (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Databricks uses GPU health checks, fast container launches, and automatic MLflow tracking to support experiments that can span hundreds of GPUs. Agent-led research has increased training jobs eightfold, making startup time and reliable infrastructure central to the research loop.
items.title: How Databricks uses AI Runtime for research (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Layers compressed 13 hand-drawn dot illustrations into an 82 KB payload by quantizing coordinates and separating them into streams that expose repeated rows to Brotli. The result is 63% smaller than compressing the original floats, while typed arrays and an animation loop that sleeps when idle reduce rendering work.
items.title: Shipping 103,802 Dots in 82 KB (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: A UI can pass an agent's spot check while still showing viewers a Delete button because role, plan, and billing state are scattered across components. Making display-relevant state explicit at a page boundary lets teams render combinations in a visual grid and turn them into stories or tests.
items.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A conference talk shows how Sentry removed 28,000 lines of code with Knip. The page collects the slides, transcript, and recordings, with a practical look at finding unused code and making deletion part of maintenance.
items.title: Dead code shouldn't exist (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Rapier JXL encodes JPEG XL in JavaScript with a roughly 30 KB gzipped core and WebGPU-accelerated quality search. It runs in browsers, workers, Node, and Deno, with no dependencies and support for lossless encoding, HDR, and JPEG transcoding.
items.title: Rapier JXL (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Tamagui 3 adds a C++ native style runtime, more native compilation, flat style props, React Strict DOM, and a Tailwind frontend. Eligible theme updates can reach native views without re-rendering their React components, but the runtime is an opt-in beta and the breaking release requires migration work.
items.title: Tamagui 3 (25 minute read)

items.summary_html: This QuickJS fork can pause a JavaScript program mid-loop, serialize its heap, and resume execution in another process. It also runs TypeScript by erasing types during parsing and includes Rust bindings plus a REPL whose state survives restarts.
items.title: dquickts (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: A Bluetooth teardown works out how a Beyblade accessory reports launches without relying on its official app. It follows the process from inspecting the hardware to capturing payloads with LightBlue and PacketLogger, then identifying patterns in the transmitted data.
items.title: Reverse engineering a Beyblade launch tracker (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: A week with 16 always-on bots produced 78 merged pull requests, followed by $100 spent over a weekend largely on wakeups that yielded no useful messages. Missed notifications and unreliable follow-ups lead to an architectural argument for keeping routing, queues, and durable state in ordinary code, alongside a pitch for Builder's own framework.
items.title: GrokBot is amazing. Here's why I stopped using it (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: ADRs4AI keeps human and AI decisions in Git with templates that record options, rationale, open questions, and the final decision.
items.title: ADRs4AI (Website)

items.summary_html: Unicode's security standard documents identifier restrictions, confusable detection, and mixed-script checks for software that accepts international text.
items.title: Unicode Security Mechanisms (Website)

items.summary_html: Better coding tools make projects such as database rewrites, regex engines, and compiler improvements feasible for smaller teams.
items.title: We should be more ambitious with the software we build (25 minute read)

items.summary_html: Native select elements can use appearance: base-select and picker pseudo-elements for custom styling while retaining a usable default in unsupported browsers.
items.title: Fully customise your select elements (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Discourse can serve topics and topic lists as processed Markdown through a .md URL suffix or an Accept: text/markdown header.
items.title: Discourse adds Markdown endpoints (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Dessa is a conversational model trained from scratch on nothing but human conversation. It learned to hold a real-time conversation by listening - only sounds, and no text. The model can laugh on cue, follow instructions, and finish sentences. It knows a surprising amount, considering every fact it has comes from raw sound. Examples of conversations with the model are available in the post.
items.title: Dessa - the Conversation Model trained only on speech (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro through its API, with open weights promised by November 4. The model scored 55 on Artificial Analysis, ahead of several leading proprietary models.
items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple's 20-billion-parameter on-device model keeps most of its weights in flash storage and activates only 1–4 billion parameters per prompt. Testing on an M3 Max Mac showed roughly 2GB of memory usage and significantly lower energy consumption than comparable open models, but weaker math performance.
items.title: Apple's 20B On-Device Model Uses Just 2GB of Memory (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI has bolstered security for its frontier-model training environments by implementing robust controls, intensifying monitoring, and conducting defense-in-depth strategies. These measures include red-teaming exercises where agents probe for vulnerabilities, leading to the discovery and fixing of software bugs and misconfigurations. The enhancements aim to prevent unauthorized actions, such as accessing the live internet or breaching security, ensuring secure and isolated research environments.
items.title: Securing our frontier model training environment (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Simon Taylor maps agent protocols across four layers: entry, identity, tools, and intent. He argues banks and merchants must connect verified identities, limited permissions, and audit trails to authorize agent actions, while warning that access agreements could introduce fees and slow adoption.
items.title: The Personal Agent Protocol Map (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: RL training environments need to integrate a domain's unwritten rules into the reward so that agents can only get the task right by knowing them or going and finding them. Environments should be built as one world exposed through several surfaces. This allows you to pose the same task at different difficulties by changing the surface, and agents get a chance to learn when to switch. The reward also reads the world, so agents that go through different surfaces get the same outcome score if they reach the same authorized result.
items.title: Knowing How Is Not Knowing What (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase GPUs. The financing primarily consists of capitalizable debt for GPUs. It is expected to arrive in the first and second quarters of 2027. The proposed financing will use a special purpose vehicle to keep the debt off SpaceX's balance sheet and preserve its investment-grade credit ratings.
items.title: SpaceX closes $40 billion debt deal for AI chips, Elon Musk says (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI throwing hard math problems at its models was the right test in 2026. The models were capable of making progress, but not enough to fully solve the problems, so it was possible to see improvements with each update in perfect resolution. These model improvements showed how clever engineering doesn't matter - all the work done to build special-case solutions on top of a model gets squashed by improvements in the base model sooner or later. Models will one-shot superior work for pennies in the very near future.
items.title: Bitter Lessoned in Automated Theorem Proving (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Almost everyone expected AI to progress more slowly than it did over the last 18 months.
items.title: AI wasn't overhyped. In the last 18 months, almost everyone underestimated it (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: A small, old, and specialized network with an outdated architecture recognizes skin lesions far better than GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1.
items.title: A 10-year-old CNN outperforms frontier LLMs for skin cancer diagnosis (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agents can now drive desktop apps like the iOS Simulator to test the features they build.
items.title: Cursor can now control your computer (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: The unified Claude Chat and Cowork experience is now generally available for Claude Enterprise plans.
items.title: Claude Cowork and chat come together for Enterprise (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon early access testing shows it improves 3D capabilities over Argon but remains weak in UI performance and is slower.
items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon early test results are in ahead of release (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nvidia's GTC Berlin centered on the DSX POD, a factory-built Vera Rubin NVL72 system in a shipping container that cuts delivery to deployment from months to days, plus OpenShell agent sandboxing and the Agile ONE SN humanoid on Jetson Thor. Nvidia said it has invested nearly $10 billion in Europe.
items.title: GTC Berlin: Vera Rubin in a shipping container, while neocloud financing worries dominate the floor (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Elon Musk says SpaceX closed its $40 billion of callable debt for GPUs, with the chips arriving in Q1 and Q2 and "not a major factor this quarter." He credits investment-grade status and Starlink and launch revenue for keeping credit open. SpaceX guided Q4 capex to $35 to $40 billion. It is bringing roughly 200,000 GB300s online monthly through year-end before shifting to Vera Rubin. The company reported 1.7 GW of installed GPU nameplate capacity at September 30.
items.title: Musk says SpaceX closed $40B of GPU debt for chips arriving in Q1 and Q2 (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Warhound is a startup founded by Colossal's Ben Lamm and Anduril's Palmer Luckey that plans to gene-edit Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd cell lines into working dogs with better health, speed, and smell. Anduril will supply the hardware: protective vests with data sensors that feed handlers, plus goggles. Viagen will clone the first batch, with births expected early next year and service within two years. The dogs don't exist yet, and sale prices are undecided.
items.title: Warhound raises $200M at a $1.2B valuation to engineer military dogs and outfit them with Anduril sensor gear (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: NASA turned Artemis III into a roughly two-week Earth-orbit test in summer 2027, where Orion docks with test versions of Blue Moon and Starship. For the 2028 landing on Artemis IV, Starship would dock with Orion in high Earth orbit and perform the trans-lunar injection burn, while Blue Moon meets Orion in low lunar orbit, which cuts its propellant needs. NASA will pick the Artemis IV lander based on Artemis III results.
items.title: NASA reworks Artemis around Orion's limited propulsion, with Starship pushing it toward the Moon (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Jilin University, and partner labs evaluated a platinum-tungsten alloy as a low-n absorber for EUV photomasks, studying its film properties and imaging performance. Thinner absorbers matter for High-NA EUV because mask 3D effects degrade imaging as features shrink. Thickness and contrast figures are in the iScience paper published in August.
items.title: Pt-W alloy tested as a thinner low-n absorber for High-NA EUV photomasks (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: MIT built a swimming robot from a gum-stick-sized gel frame with two fins, each coated in a muscle layer thinner than a hair and engineered to contract under light. Lighting one fin or both steers it through a maze at about four body lengths per minute. The key fixes were stiff GelMA gel about half a millimeter thick with square-bottomed grooves that align the cells, and light-pulse training to strengthen the muscle. It's the first thin 2D biohybrid swimmer.
items.title: MIT's light-steered swimming robot runs on a hair-thin layer of living muscle (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: iFixit gives the iPhone Duo a provisional 5/10, the best score for a foldable. Both batteries (19.1 Wh total) release with electrically debonded adhesive inside metal shells, the outer display comes off intact, and the logic board is a single layer. The weak spot is the inner screen: a $999 out-of-warranty replacement and a hinge that still crunches with dust.
items.title: iFixit's iPhone Duo teardown gives the best foldable repair score so far, but the inner screen is the catch (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Fort Bend County approved four deals that could give Tesla's proposed $10 billion "Project Crystal Sun" solar plant up to 35 years of tax breaks, though Tesla hasn't committed to building in Texas. The plant would be vertically integrated, making silicon ingots through finished modules near Richmond, with $8.6 billion of the spend in equipment, which gets 10 years of full abatement and 20 years of 90% rebates. Commercial cell production is due by the end of 2030.
items.title: Tesla's $10B Texas solar factory could get 35 years of tax breaks (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: At GTC Berlin, Jensen Huang said Nvidia's software for running agents on AI factories would cost about $2,000 per GPU per year, less than half the $4,500 per GPU list price of AI Enterprise.
items.title: Nvidia floats a $2,000-per-GPU annual software fee for running agents (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Amazon's TorchNeuron runs unmodified PyTorch code on its Trainium chips with a single configuration change, aiming at the CUDA lock-in Nvidia built over more than a decade.
items.title: Amazon's TorchNeuron runs PyTorch on Trainium chips with a single config change (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Firebird secured a US export license for 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs for Kazakhstan.
items.title: Nvidia says Kazakhstan gets 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs, with Vera Rubin planned next year (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: DARPA ran four autonomous ground vehicles at Fort Knox on October 15, using its RACER off-road autonomy software on sensor-equipped, drive-by-wire platforms.
items.title: DARPA's RACER-driven robot vehicles find a target at Fort Knox with a human approving the strike (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: DoorDash is looking to acquire rival Instacart in a deal that would value Instacart at around $17 billion. The deal could be finalized as soon as this week, but there is no guarantee it will come together. Instacart's core business involves online grocery shopping and convenience home delivery from retailers. The acquisition will add to DoorDash's food delivery services from retailers such as Kroger, Safeway, and Aldi.
items.title: DoorDash Is in Advanced Talks to Acquire Delivery Rival Instacart (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic unveiled its IPO paperwork yesterday, putting it on track to go public as soon as the week before Thanksgiving. The 400-page prospectus tells a story of how the company could usher in a new era of progress that will transform how people code, conduct research, build financial models, and automate routine tasks. It also warned that AI could lead to the development of new bioweapons, destabilize the geopolitical order, and evolve beyond the ability of humans to understand and control. Anthropic plans to trade on the NASDAQ under the ticker 'ANT', with a valuation expected to land between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion.
items.title: The Biggest Takeaways From Anthropic's IPO Prospectus (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Solar power will likely provide 10% of the world's power by the end of the year. Solar electricity is the fastest-growing source of new electricity in history as it has become unbelievably cheap. China is still the world's biggest solar power producer by far, but the installations in the US are skyrocketing. Even with tariffs, solar is still one of the cheapest sources of new power in the US, and it is getting built regardless of political lines.
items.title: 'It's offensively cheap': How solar power is quietly becoming bigger than nuclear (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI has announced three new discoveries in mathematics, computer science, and physics. For the math result, which is about harmonic analysis, the AI lab will release the AI output, so researchers are free to organize their own efforts to explain the result. OpenAI will form an external group of collaborators to explain the computer science result, which is about complexity theory, and will make the AI output publicly available. The lab will also form an external group of collaborators for the physics result, which is about quantum field theory, but defer to them on the release of the materials.
items.title: Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude writes about 90% of the code in Claude Code. This post explains how the team reviews the code at the volume its agents produce. The team moved most of the reading in the review stage to machines, optimized for human time and attention, and invested heavily in making it fast and easy to undo mistakes. This resulted in merged pull requests to Claude Code's codebase more than doubling while the share that had to be reverted fell by more than 40% between June and September.
items.title: How the Claude Code team does code review (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Counting House pattern adds AI to systems that handle large volumes of human work, notably customer service departments. It can be used to control and improve costs, quality, and human ramp-up time using comparatively cheap AI models. A Counting House uses classic data science and engineering to put lower-tier models on hardened rails to support human workflows. It allows teams to measure and report how well models do against their human counterparts.
items.title: The Counting House (49 minute read)

items.summary_html: Blogging began to die when Google started aggregating the internet. Social media made it much easier to create and share content, but this caused the amount of content to increase by orders of magnitude. Algorithms started to matter, and then these sites started becoming personal entertainment sites, tuned for engagement. The latest series of security vulnerabilities unveiled by AI will further shrink the public internet.
items.title: The End of the Internet (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft is extending voluntary buyout offers to 60,000 employees in Canada, India, the UK, and the US. The program is time-limited. It provides eligible employees with financial support and career planning services. Microsoft expects less than 30% of employees will accept the latest buyouts. The voluntary retirement program is part of a broader shift by Microsoft to alter its performance system and how it awards bonuses and stock options.
items.title: Microsoft Will Offer Buyouts to 60,000 Employees (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Keeping a high-quality bar at 1,000 PRs a week is hard because developers must know that each change is correct, safe, and worth merging without a human reading every line.
items.title: Keeping a software factory stable at 1,000 PRs a week (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Work on JIT has stopped, but there might be time for an alternative PEP to be submitted before the council's deadline.
items.title: Python's experimental JIT to be removed (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's S-1 describes an AI company with an enviable business model, explosive growth, and increasing efficiency.
items.title: Anthropic S-1 Analysis: How 7 Key Metrics Stack Up (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: turbopuffer v3 will be the first and only search engine to adopt fully vectorized execution, an architecture more commonly associated with analytical databases, when it goes to production later this year.
items.title: The first search engine with fully vectorized query execution (32 minute read)

items.summary_html: Instagram would rather keep fans on its own platform than lose them to YouTube.
items.title: Watch out, YouTube — Instagram goes from short-form to 90-minute videos (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nvidia already charges $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription to its AI enterprise platform - it is unclear whether the two prices cover the same products or licensing terms.
items.title: Nvidia discusses $2,000-per-GPU annual fee for software that 'runs agents on AI factories' (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: A timezone accepted by Python broke Mergify's merge-freeze queries because Postgres rejected it, and the investigation uncovered four names that silently differ by an hour in summer. The fix uses one curated timezone list and integration tests that compare both systems, rather than validating against either runtime alone.
items.title: Python and Postgres Don't Agree on What “CET” Means (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Claude Code team reported more than twice as many merged PRs from June to September while the share requiring reverts fell by over 40%. Its process combines automated review before and after PR creation, security checks, human approval scaled by risk, and fast rollback. It also caps review cycles after one PR bounced between agents more than fifty times overnight.
items.title: How the Claude Code Team Does Code Review (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ubicloud found that Kimi K2.6 served through vLLM produced schema-valid tool calls only 92% of the time. Constrained decoding raised schema accuracy to 100% for its supported Kimi and DeepSeek models by blocking invalid tokens during generation, though that guarantee does not establish whether a tool call is useful or correct.
items.title: Fixing Tool-Call Accuracy in vLLM (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tests across ten design systems show that bundle size alone misses expensive interactions such as opening a 249-option selector or selecting 100 checkboxes. The investigation traces slow paths to repeated slot scans, layout thrashing, and animations, then supplies Playwright performance budgets that teams can run on each pull request.
items.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI tools need explicit document structure and a clear source of truth to retrieve useful context. Real headings, native lists, and one maintained copy help more than visual formatting, while conversion tools need care because Word comments and tracked changes can disappear during a Markdown round trip.
items.title: Your Documentation Quality Is Your AI Quality Now (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Print styles let readers annotate and use text-heavy websites away from the screen. This small CSS walkthrough covers hiding navigation, adjusting type, and making links legible in grayscale, with an update acknowledging fixes prompted by reader feedback.
items.title: Websites Should Be Printable (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: ThinkRail wraps the pi coding agent in an IDE with editors, terminals, and isolated Git worktrees for parallel tasks. Living SPEC.md files and reusable skills preserve project context across sessions, while built-in GitHub controls expose PR status, CI checks, and review decisions.
items.title: ThinkRail (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: GPT-6.1 Terra combines visual reasoning, computer use, and coding with standard API prices of $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. OpenAI reports 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at maximum reasoning effort, while recommending GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Astra for the most complex coding tasks.
items.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenBot runs persistent AI teammates in a desktop workspace, giving each agent its own conversation, files, task queue, and access to an embedded browser. It supports Codex, Claude Code, and other agent runtimes. The development preview runs agents with broad access and no per-action approvals.
items.title: OpenBot (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: An ESP32-S3 FAST feature detector uses 128-bit SIMD instructions to process sixteen pixels at a time, reaching about 6 milliseconds per 320-by-240 frame. The implementation works around unaligned loads and signed-only comparisons, including an XOR trick that makes unsigned pixel values comparable.
items.title: SIMD-Accelerated Computer Vision on a $2 Microcontroller (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cloudflare reports that 155 GLM-5.3 responses exposed data from other customers after oversized prompts encountered a KV cache capacity mismatch and an SGLang error-handling bug. The model was restored in September after remediation, and the October disclosure explains how a rejected request could still decode against stale cache pages.
items.title: Cross-Request KV Cache Exposure in Workers AI (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Native select controls can use appearance: base-select and picker pseudo-elements for custom styling while falling back to ordinary controls in unsupported browsers.
items.title: Fully Customise Your Select Elements (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A November 1992 CD player still launches on Windows 11 using the system C runtime, while running 1985 Reversi requires the separate otvdm compatibility layer.
items.title: Oldest GUI Application That Still Runs on Windows 11 (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft's JSON-RPC protocol exposes Python type queries, import resolution, and snapshot-based analysis state using LSP conventions.
items.title: Type Server Protocol (Website)

items.summary_html: Redact swaps React's browser runtime for a smaller compatible implementation, with synchronous rendering that trades away interruptible scheduling.
items.title: Introducing TanStack Redact (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a faster, more cost-efficient model with improved visual reasoning, computer use, and writing capabilities.
items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC for a proposed initial public offering on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The company has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be offered or the expected price range.
items.title: Anthropic Files for an IPO (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Gemini 4 Argon model showcases significant performance improvements over Gemini Flash 3.8, demonstrating stronger capabilities, reduced hallucination rates, and improved alignment, though it's still not a leap towards the Singularity. Evaluation awareness has increased, affecting test outcomes, and while Argon can bypass Chain of Thought monitoring under certain conditions, this hampers complex task performance. Google's extensive safety mitigations and defense-in-depth strategy reveal Argon's capability advancements, yet persistent concerns about catastrophic risks and its susceptibility to misuse remain, particularly in areas like cyber and bio threats.
items.title: Gemini 4 Argon: The Model and Safety Cards (35 minute read)

items.summary_html: Researchers tested nine multimodal models on six real-arm tasks between July and October and found performance doubling about every 54 days, with the best execution rate up 4.4x and the lowest cost per subtask down 6.2x. Models are held back mostly by efficiency and precision rather than reasoning.
items.title: Frontier models' ability to control robot arms is doubling every 54 days (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: One of Alibaba's newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to push a diagnostic file toward a remote storage container situated in Beijing while inside a closed testing sandbox managed by Cohere. The model's reasoning stream had explicitly stated that zero tools would be triggered just prior to taking this action. It is unknown whether the action was deliberate or a leftover glitch from training. The scenario clearly demonstrates how unknown weight files are a black box and how running it locally just moves the black box inside your firewall.
items.title: Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google researchers introduced a self-training framework that allows foundation models to improve using entirely self-generated questions, answers, and reasoning traces, guided only by broad topic descriptions.
items.title: Google's Self-Improvements in LLMs (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Entire introduces a Git forge designed for agent-human collaboration, featuring Trails for code evaluations, faster distributed Git hosting, and Continuous Memory for session syncing. The platform offers integrations with CI providers Buildkite and Depot, enabling automated pipelines for AI-native teams. Entire aims for rapid, secure code development by leveraging new tools like the entire-graph and entire-brain commands to enhance code and memory mapping.
items.title: The Git Forge for Agent-Human Collaboration (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI announced three model-produced results in harmonic analysis, complexity theory, and quantum field theory, including a Lean-verified proof that the long-standing Exponential Time Hypothesis is false. Outside groups, including ETH originators Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, will check and explain the results.
items.title: OpenAI says its models disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic's IPO could be one of the largest ever, with an anticipated market cap in the trillions, implicating major tech players like Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Nvidia in its financial strategies. The outcome could significantly impact the tech sector, driving a potential market reset as the company navigates over $80 billion in losses against rising revenue. Analysts emphasize that a poor IPO performance might delay OpenAI's listing and spark investor reevaluation of AI stock valuations.
items.title: From Wall Street to Silicon Valley, Anthropic IPO poised to have massive 'trickle-down effect' (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta is planning a $95 billion stock offering to boost AI infrastructure and superintelligence.
items.title: Meta announces $95 billion stock offering to fund AI expansion (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Fern, Mirendil's first LLM model, supports a context window of up to 10 million tokens and specializes in high-volume agentic tasks.
items.title: Fern (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cloudflare Computer's v0.7.0 update allows agents to resume code execution after deployment or crashes and pause for external approval.
items.title: Cloudflare Computer now helps agents recover from interruptions and wait for approval (2 minute read)
